bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts exhausted time or context while misreading the position-transformed byte stream as direct opcodes and repeatedly implementing or probing incorrect encodings. A separate broken setup forced every attempt to spend a turn repairing execute permission before it could use the VM.
change: Repair in the environment: preserve execute permission on the supplied VM so the instruction’s documented ./vm program.bin signal is immediately reachable. Because every attempt reached and repaired this defect, no additional simplification is added until the repaired task is measured.
restore: Restore the original non-executable file mode only when reverting the broken setup; there is no hint or supplied retained-skill work to withdraw.
prediction: The change addresses the failing chmod/setup action and enables immediate execution of examples and probes. A fresh container can invoke /app/vm directly; this is refuted if it still returns permission denied. Since the dominant encoding decision is intentionally retained, only a small shift is predicted.
